title.zh: 卷七十八 列傳第二十八: 于志寧 高季輔 張行成
title.en: Volume 78 Biographies 28: Yu Zhining, Gao Jifu, Zhang Xingcheng
title.raw: 卷七十八 列傳第二十八: 于志寧 高季輔 張行成 Volume 78 Biographies 28: Yu Zhining, Gao Jifu, Zhang Xingcheng

sentences.zh: 於志寧 高季輔 張行成 族孫易之 昌宗

translations.literal: Yu Zhining, Gao Jifu, Zhang Xingcheng; clan grandsons Yizhi and Changzong.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhining, Gao Jifu, and Zhang Xingcheng; their clansmen Yizhi and Changzong.

sentences.zh: 於志寧，雍州高陵人，周太師燕文公謹之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yu Zhining was a man of Gaoling in Yong Province, the great-grandson of Yan Duke Wen, Grand Tutor Jin of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zhining, a native of Gaoling in Yong Province, was the great-grandson of Jin, Duke Wen of Yan and Grand Tutor of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 父宣道，隋內史舍人。

translations.literal: His father Xuandao was a secretary in the inner secretariat under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuandao had served as a secretary in the Sui inner secretariat.

sentences.zh: 志寧，大業末為冠氏縣長，時山東群盜起，乃棄官歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Zhining, at the end of the Daye era, was magistrate of Guanxian County; when bandits rose throughout Shandong, he abandoned his office and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign, Zhining was magistrate of Guanxian County. When bandit armies rose across Shandong, he resigned his post and went home.

sentences.zh: 高祖將入關，率群從於長春宮迎接，高祖以其有名於時，甚加禮遇，授銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was about to enter the Pass, he led his kinsmen to welcome him at Changchun Palace; Gaozu, because he was renowned in the age, greatly honored him and appointed him Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: As Gaozu prepared to enter the Pass, Zhining led his kinsmen to Changchun Palace to welcome him. Gaozu, knowing his reputation, treated him with exceptional courtesy and appointed him Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 太宗為渭北道行軍元帥，召補記室，與殷開山等參贊軍謀。

translations.literal: When Taizong was commander-in-chief of the Weibei campaign army, he summoned him to fill the post of recorder and, with Yin Kaishan and others, assisted in military planning.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong served as commander-in-chief on the Weibei campaign, he appointed Zhining recorder of his staff, and Zhining joined Yin Kaishan and others in advising on military strategy.

sentences.zh: 及太宗為秦王、天策上將，志寧累授天策府從事中郎，每侍從征伐，兼文學館學士。

translations.literal: When Taizong became Prince of Qin and Celestial Stratagem General-in-Chief, Zhining was repeatedly appointed attendant gentleman of the Celestial Stratagem Bureau; he attended on every campaign and also served as a scholar of the Literary Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong became Prince of Qin and Celestial Stratagem General-in-Chief, Zhining rose through appointments as attendant gentleman of the Celestial Stratagem Bureau. He accompanied every campaign and also held a post as scholar of the Literary Academy.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，累遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan he was promoted in succession to vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan (629), he was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太宗命貴臣內殿宴，怪不見志寧，或奏曰：「敕召三品已上，志寧非三品，所以不來。」

translations.literal: Taizong ordered eminent ministers to a banquet in the inner hall and wondered that Zhining did not appear; someone reported, "The edict summoned those of third rank and above; Zhining is not third rank, and therefore did not come."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned eminent ministers to a banquet in the inner hall and wondered why Zhining was absent. Someone reported, "Your summons called for officials of third rank and above. Zhining is below third rank, so he did not come."

sentences.zh: 太宗特令預宴，即加授散騎常侍，行太子左庶子。

translations.literal: Taizong specially ordered him to attend the banquet and at once additionally appointed him irregular attendant-in-ordinary, acting left vice director of the crown prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered him to attend anyway and immediately promoted him to irregular attendant-in-ordinary, with the acting title of left vice director of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 累封黎陽縣公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed in succession as Duke of Liyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in succession as Duke of Liyang County.

sentences.zh: 時議者欲立七廟，以涼武昭王為始祖，房玄齡等皆以為然。

translations.literal: At the time debaters wished to establish seven ancestral temples, taking Martial and Illustrious King of Liang as the founding ancestor; Fang Xuanling and others all considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some officials proposed establishing seven ancestral temples with the Martial and Illustrious King of Liang as the founding ancestor, and Fang Xuanling and others agreed.

sentences.zh: 志寧獨建議以為武昭遠祖，非王業所因，不可為始祖。

translations.literal: Zhining alone submitted a proposal holding that Martial and Illustrious was a remote ancestor and not the source from which royal enterprise arose, and could not serve as founding ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining alone argued that the Martial and Illustrious King was a remote forebear, not the source of the dynasty's rise, and therefore could not be named founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 太宗又以功臣為代襲刺史，志寧以今古事殊，恐非久安之道，上疏爭之。

translations.literal: Taizong also wished to make meritorious officials hereditary prefects generation after generation; Zhining, holding that present and past affairs differed, feared this was not a path of long peace, and submitted a memorial disputing it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong also planned to make meritorious officials hereditary prefects. Zhining argued that times had changed and that such a policy would not secure lasting peace, and he submitted a memorial objecting to the plan.

sentences.zh: 皆從志寧所議。

translations.literal: All followed what Zhining had proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted Zhining's position on both matters.

sentences.zh: 太宗因謂志寧曰：「古者太子既生，士負之，即置輔弼。

translations.literal: Taizong thereupon said to Zhining, "In antiquity, once the crown prince was born, a scholar would carry him on his back, and tutors were at once appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then told Zhining, "In antiquity, as soon as a crown prince was born, a scholar would carry him on his back and tutors were appointed immediately.

sentences.zh: 昔成王幼小，周、召為師傅，日聞正道，習以成性。

translations.literal: Formerly, when King Cheng was young, the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao served as his masters, daily hearing the correct Way until it became habit through practice.
translations.idiomatic: When King Cheng of Zhou was still a child, the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao served as his tutors, so that he heard the right path every day until it became second nature.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子既幼少，卿當輔之以正道，無使邪僻開其心。

translations.literal: Now that the crown prince is still young, you should assist him with the correct Way and not let perverse paths open his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Our crown prince is still very young. You must guide him along the right path and keep depraved influences from taking root in his mind.

sentences.zh: 勉之無怠，當稱所委，官賞可不次而得也。」

translations.literal: Urge him without slackening; you will be equal to what is entrusted, and office and reward may be obtained out of regular order."
translations.idiomatic: Press on without slackening. If you prove worthy of this charge, rank and rewards may come to you out of turn."

sentences.zh: 志寧以承乾數虧禮度，志在匡救，撰《諫苑》二十捲諷之。

translations.literal: Zhining, because Chengan repeatedly fell short in ritual and measure, set his will on correction and rescue, and composed twenty scrolls of Admonitory Garden to admonish him by indirection.
translations.idiomatic: Because Crown Prince Chengan repeatedly breached ritual propriety, Zhining set out to correct him and wrote twenty scrolls of the Admonitory Garden as an indirect remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 太宗大悅，賜黃金十斤、絹三百匹。

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly pleased and bestowed ten catties of gold and three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was greatly pleased and rewarded him with ten catties of gold and three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 十四年，兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he additionally served as steward of the crown prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year (640) he was additionally appointed steward of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 明年，以母憂解。

translations.literal: The next year he was released on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 尋起復本官，屢表請終喪禮，太宗遣中書侍郎岑文本就宅敦諭之曰：「忠孝不併，我兒須人輔弼，卿宜抑割，不可徇以私情。」

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled to his former office; he repeatedly submitted memorials asking to complete the mourning rites, and Taizong sent vice director of the Secretariat Cen Wuben to his residence to urge him earnestly, saying, "Loyalty and filial piety cannot be joined; my son needs someone to assist him—you should restrain your grief and not indulge private feeling."
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to his former post, but he repeatedly asked permission to complete the full mourning period. Taizong sent Vice Director Cen Wuben to his home to press him: "Loyalty and filial duty cannot both be fulfilled at once. My son needs a tutor. You must set grief aside and not let private feeling rule you."

sentences.zh: 志寧遂起就職。

translations.literal: Zhining thereupon rose and took up his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining then returned to office.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子承乾嘗以盛農之時，營造曲室，累月不止，所為多不法。

translations.literal: At the time Crown Prince Chengan, during the height of the farming season, had constructed secluded chambers and did not stop for many months; most of what he did was unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: Around this time Crown Prince Chengan, in the middle of the busy farming season, had been building private chambers for months on end, and much of his conduct was unlawful.

sentences.zh: 志寧上書諫曰：

translations.literal: Zhining submitted a written remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhining submitted a written remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 臣聞克儉節用，實弘道之源；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that overcoming extravagance and economizing in expenditure are truly the source of extending the Way;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that practicing thrift and restraining expenditure are the true foundations of extending the Way;

sentences.zh: 崇侈恣情，乃敗德之本。

translations.literal: exalting luxury and indulging desire are the root of ruining virtue.
translations.idiomatic: while exalting luxury and indulging every whim are the roots of ruined virtue.

sentences.zh: 是以凌雲概日，戎人於是致譏；

translations.literal: Therefore halls touching the clouds and spanning the sun drew mockery from the Rong people;
translations.idiomatic: That is why halls that touched the clouds drew mockery from the Rong;

sentences.zh: 峻宇雕牆，《夏書》以之作誡。

translations.literal: lofty halls and carved walls—the Documents of Xia took these as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: and lofty halls with carved walls became warnings recorded in the Documents of Xia.

sentences.zh: 昔趙盾匡晉，呂望師周，或勸之以節財，或諫之以厚斂，莫不盡忠以佐國，竭誠以奉君，欲茂實播於無窮，英聲被乎物聽。

translations.literal: Formerly Zhao Dun rectified Jin and Lü Wang instructed Zhou; one was urged to economize wealth, the other remonstrated against heavy exactions—none failed to exhaust loyalty in assisting the state and pour sincerity in serving the ruler, wishing solid merit to spread without end and illustrious fame to reach all who hear.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Zhao Dun set Jin aright and Lü Wang guided Zhou; one was urged to husband resources, the other warned against heavy levies. Each gave his full loyalty to the state and his full sincerity to his lord, so that solid merit might endure and a noble name reach every ear.

sentences.zh: 咸著簡策，以為美談。

translations.literal: All are recorded on bamboo and silk as fine tales.
translations.idiomatic: Their deeds are all recorded in the histories as models worth praising.

sentences.zh: 今所居東宮，隋日營建，睹之者尚譏其侈，見之者猶嘆其華。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace in which you now dwell was built in Sui days; those who behold it still mock its extravagance, and those who see it still sigh at its splendor.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace where Your Highness now lives was built in Sui times. Those who see it still mock its extravagance and sigh at its splendor.

sentences.zh: 何容此中更有修造，財帛日費，土木不停，窮斤斧之工，極磨礱之妙？

translations.literal: How can it be fitting that within it there is further construction, wealth and cloth daily spent, earth and timber unceasing, exhausting the work of axe and adze and reaching the utmost in grinding and polishing?
translations.idiomatic: How then can it be right to add still more construction inside it, spending wealth day after day, piling up earth and timber without pause, and exhausting every art of the carpenter's trade?

sentences.zh: 且丁匠官奴入內，比者曾無伏監。

translations.literal: Moreover, corvée craftsmen and official slaves enter within; recently there has been no hidden supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, corvée craftsmen and government slaves have been entering the inner quarters, and lately there has been no proper oversight.

sentences.zh: 此等或兄犯國章，或弟罹王法，往來御苑，出入禁闈，鉗鑿緣其身，槌杵在其手。

translations.literal: Among these, some brothers have violated state statutes, some younger brothers have fallen under royal law; they come and go through the imperial park and enter and leave the forbidden inner quarters, fetters and chisels upon their persons, mallets and pestles in their hands.
translations.idiomatic: Some of these men have brothers who broke state law, or younger brothers condemned under royal statute. Yet they move through the imperial park and in and out of the forbidden inner quarters, still wearing fetters and still bearing mallets in their hands.

sentences.zh: 監門本防非慮，宿衛以備不虞，直長既自不知，千牛又復不見。

translations.literal: Gatekeepers exist to guard against the unexpected, night guards to prepare for the unforeseen—yet the duty captain himself did not know, and the thousand-ox guards again did not see.
translations.idiomatic: Gatekeepers exist to guard against the unexpected, and night guards to prepare for emergencies. Yet the duty captain knew nothing of this, and the thousand-ox guards saw nothing either.

sentences.zh: 爪牙在外，廝役在內，所司何以自安，臣下豈容無懼？

translations.literal: Claws and fangs outside, menials within—how can the responsible offices rest secure? How can your subjects not be afraid?
translations.idiomatic: Armed guards stand outside while convict laborers work inside. How can the responsible offices feel secure? How can your officials not be afraid?

sentences.zh: 又鄭、衛之樂，古謂淫聲。

translations.literal: Moreover, the music of Zheng and Wei the ancients called licentious sound.
translations.idiomatic: The music of Zheng and Wei, moreover, the ancients called licentious sound.

sentences.zh: 昔朝歌之鄉，回車者墨翟；

translations.literal: Formerly at the district of Chaoge, Mozi turned his carriage back;
translations.idiomatic: When Mozi passed the district of Chaoge, he turned his carriage around;

sentences.zh: 夾谷之會，揮劍者孔丘。

translations.literal: at the meeting of Jiagu, Confucius brandished his sword.
translations.idiomatic: and at the meeting of Jiagu, Confucius drew his sword.

sentences.zh: 先聖既以為非，通賢將以為失。

translations.literal: The former sages already held these wrong; the broadly wise will likewise regard them as faults.
translations.idiomatic: The sages of old already condemned such things, and every wise man will judge them faults.

sentences.zh: 頃聞宮內，屢有鼓聲大樂，伎兒入便不出。

translations.literal: Recently it is heard that within the palace there have repeatedly been drum music and great ensembles; performers enter and do not come out.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that within the palace drums and grand ensembles sound again and again, and that performers enter and do not come out.

sentences.zh: 聞之者股慄，言之者心戰。

translations.literal: Those who hear it tremble in the thighs; those who speak of it battle in the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hear it tremble; those who speak of it do so with fear in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 往年口敕，伏請重尋，聖旨慇勤，明誡懇切。

translations.literal: In former years there was an oral edict—I humbly ask that it be sought again; the sage command was earnest, the clear admonition sincere and pressing.
translations.idiomatic: In years past Your Majesty issued an oral edict on this matter. I beg that it be consulted again. The imperial instruction was earnest and the warning clear.

sentences.zh: 在於殿下，不可不思，至於微臣，不得無懼。

translations.literal: For Your Highness it cannot go unconsidered; as for this humble subject, he cannot be without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness cannot fail to reflect on this. As for me, I cannot help but be afraid.

sentences.zh: 臣自驅馳宮闕，已積歲年，犬馬尚解識恩，木石猶能知感，所有管見，敢不盡言？

translations.literal: Your subject, since serving at the palace gates, has accumulated years; even dogs and horses still understand favor, even wood and stone can know gratitude—all that this narrow view sees, how dare I not speak fully?
translations.idiomatic: I have served at the palace gates for many years. Even dogs and horses know gratitude; even wood and stone can feel obligation. How can I withhold what my limited understanding sees?

sentences.zh: 如鑑以丹誠，則臣有生路；

translations.literal: If you mirror my cinnabar sincerity, then your subject has a path of life;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness weighs my sincere heart, I may yet live;

sentences.zh: 若責其忤旨，則臣是罪人。

translations.literal: if you blame me for opposing the intent, then your subject is a guilty man.
translations.idiomatic: if you blame me for opposing your will, then I am a guilty man.

sentences.zh: 但悅意取容，藏孫方之疾疹；

translations.literal: Yet to please the intent and win favor is what Zangsun Fang compared to a running sore;
translations.idiomatic: Yet to please and win favor is what Zangsun Fang compared to a running sore;

sentences.zh: 犯顏逆耳，《春秋》比之藥石。

translations.literal: to offend the countenance and oppose the ear, the Spring and Autumn Annals compared to medicine and stone.
translations.idiomatic: while to offend the face and speak against the ear, the Spring and Autumn Annals compared to medicine and stone.

sentences.zh: 伏望停工匠之作，罷久役之人，絕鄭、衛之音，斥群小之輩，則三善允備，萬國作貞矣。

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will halt the work of craftsmen, dismiss those long in service, cut off the sounds of Zheng and Wei, and expel the crowd of petty men—then the three excellences will be fully prepared and the ten thousand states will take you as their standard.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that you halt the craftsmen's work, release those long in service, cut off the music of Zheng and Wei, and drive away petty men. Then the three excellences will be complete and the myriad states will have their standard.

sentences.zh: 承乾不納。

translations.literal: Chengan did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Chengan did not heed the advice.

sentences.zh: 承乾又令閹官多在左右，志寧上書諫曰：

translations.literal: Chengan again kept many eunuch officials at his side; Zhining submitted a written remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chengan also kept many eunuchs close at hand. Zhining submitted another written remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 臣聞堯稱稽古，功著於搜揚；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Yao was called one who examined antiquity, his merit shown in searching out and raising up;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Yao was praised for examining antiquity, his merit shown in searching out and elevating talent;

sentences.zh: 舜曰聰明，績彰於去惡。

translations.literal: Shun was called perspicacious, his achievement manifest in removing the evil.
translations.idiomatic: and that Shun was called perspicacious, his achievement manifest in removing the wicked.

sentences.zh: 然開元立極，布政辨方，莫不旌賁英賢，驅除不肖。

translations.literal: Yet in opening the source and establishing the pole, spreading government and distinguishing directions, none failed to display and honor worthy men and drive out the unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in founding an age and setting the cardinal directions of rule, every sage ruler honored the worthy and expelled the unworthy.

sentences.zh: 理亂之本，咸在於茲。

translations.literal: The root of order and disorder lies entirely in this.
translations.idiomatic: The root of order and disorder lies entirely in this.

sentences.zh: 況閹宦之徒，體非全氣，更蕃階闥，左右宮闈，托親近以立威權，假出納以為禍福。

translations.literal: Moreover, the class of castrated palace attendants, their bodies not possessing full vital breath, repeatedly pass through the gate-towers and attend at the left and right of the palace inner quarters, relying on closeness to establish authority and borrowing control of what goes in and out to become fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: As for eunuchs, their bodies are incomplete, yet they pass again and again through the gate-towers and wait at your side within the palace. They use intimacy to build power and control access to make or ruin men's fortunes.

sentences.zh: 昔易牙被任，變起齊邦；

translations.literal: Formerly, when Yiya was entrusted, upheaval arose in the state of Qi;
translations.idiomatic: When Yiya was entrusted with power, upheaval arose in Qi;

sentences.zh: 張讓執鈞，亂生漢室。

translations.literal: when Zhang Rang held the balance, disorder was born in the house of Han.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhang Rang held the scales of power, disorder was born in the Han house.

sentences.zh: 伊戾為詐，宋國受其殃；

translations.literal: Yili practiced deceit and the state of Song received its calamity;
translations.idiomatic: Yili practiced deceit, and Song suffered for it;

sentences.zh: 趙高作奸，秦氏鐘其弊。

translations.literal: Zhao Gao wrought treachery and the house of Qin tolled its ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gao wrought treachery, and the house of Qin tolled out its ruin.

sentences.zh: 加以弘、石用事，京、賈則連首受誅；

translations.literal: Added to this, when Hong and Shi held power, Jing and Jia were beheaded one after another;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, when Hong and Shi held power, Jing and Jia were beheaded in succession;

sentences.zh: 王、曹掌權，何、竇則踵武被戮。

translations.literal: when Wang and Cao grasped authority, He and Dou followed in their steps and were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: when Wang and Cao grasped authority, He and Dou followed them to the execution ground.

sentences.zh: 遂使縉紳重足，宰司屏氣。

translations.literal: Thereby girdled sashes stood with feet together and chief ministers held their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials stood with feet together, and chief ministers held their breath.

sentences.zh: 然順其情者，則榮逮幼沖；

translations.literal: Yet those who followed their intent gained glory reaching even the infant in swaddling;
translations.idiomatic: Those who pleased them won glory even in infancy;

sentences.zh: 迕其意者，則災及襁褓。

translations.literal: those who went against their intent suffered disaster reaching even the babe in cradle-clothes.
translations.idiomatic: those who crossed them brought disaster even on babes in the cradle.

sentences.zh: 爰暨高齊都鄴，亦弊閹官。

translations.literal: Down to when Gaoji of Qi made Ye its capital, eunuch officials were again a bane.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi made Ye its capital, eunuchs again became a plague.

sentences.zh: 鄧長顒位至侍中，陳德信爵隆開府，外干朝政，內預宴私，宗枝藉其吹噓，重臣仰其鼻息。

translations.literal: Deng Changying reached the post of palace attendant, Chen Dexin ennobled to open mansion; outside they interfered in court government, inside they took part in private banquets; imperial clansmen relied on their breath and puff, great ministers looked up to their nostril's breath.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Changying rose to palace attendant, Chen Dexin to the rank of lord with an open mansion. They meddled in court affairs by day and joined private banquets by night. Imperial clansmen courted their favor, and great ministers watched their every breath.

sentences.zh: 罪積山嶽，靡掛於刑書；

translations.literal: Crimes piled like mountains and hills, yet none were entered in the penal registers;
translations.idiomatic: Their crimes piled like mountains, yet none appeared in the penal registers;

sentences.zh: 功無涓塵，已勒於鐘鼎，富逾金穴，財甚銅山。

translations.literal: merit without a speck of dust was already carved on bells and tripods; wealth exceeded the golden cave, property surpassed the bronze mountain.
translations.idiomatic: their merit not a speck of dust was already carved on bells and tripods; their wealth exceeded the fabled golden cave and their property the bronze mountain.

sentences.zh: 是以家起怨嗟，人懷憤嘆。

translations.literal: Therefore households rose in lament, and men harbored indignant sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Households groaned in resentment, and men sighed in anger.

sentences.zh: 骨鯁之士，語不見聽；

translations.literal: Men of backbone and gills—their words were not heard;
translations.idiomatic: Straight-speaking men were not heard;

sentences.zh: 謇諤之臣，言必被斥。

translations.literal: frank and outspoken ministers—when they spoke they were surely rejected.
translations.idiomatic: and frank remonstrators were always turned away.

sentences.zh: 齊都顛覆，職此之由。

translations.literal: The overthrow of Qi's capital was chiefly due to this.
translations.idiomatic: The fall of Qi's capital came chiefly from this.

sentences.zh: 向使任諒直之臣，退佞給之士，據趙、魏之地，擁漳、滏之兵，修德行仁，養政施化，何區區周室而敢窺覦者焉！

translations.literal: If only they had employed straightforward and upright ministers, dismissed fawning and compliant men, held the lands of Zhao and Wei, and mustered the troops of Zhang and Fu, cultivated virtue and practiced benevolence, nourished government and spread transformation—how could the petty house of Zhou have dared to cast covetous eyes!
translations.idiomatic: Had they instead employed upright ministers, dismissed fawning flatterers, held the lands of Zhao and Wei, and mustered the armies of the Zhang and Fu rivers, cultivating virtue and practicing benevolence, who would have dared cast a covetous eye on the house of Zhou?

sentences.zh: 然杜漸防萌，古人所以遠禍；

translations.literal: Yet to stop the gradual and guard the sprouting is how the ancients kept disaster far off;
translations.idiomatic: Stopping evil while it is still slight is how the ancients kept disaster far away;

sentences.zh: 以大喻小，先哲於焉取則。

translations.literal: to use the large to admonish the small—former sages took their standard here.
translations.idiomatic: and using the large to warn the small is a lesson the sages drew from such cases.

sentences.zh: 伏惟殿下道茂重離，德光守器，憲章古始，祖述前修，欲使休譽遠聞，英聲遐暢。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Highness's Way flourishes in Double Li, your virtue illumines the guarded vessel; you take the statutes of antiquity's beginning and follow the accomplishments of former cultivators, wishing to make fine reputation heard far and illustrious fame spread to distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's Way flourishes in the second son, your virtue illumines the heir's vessel. You take antiquity as your statute and former sages as your models, wishing your fine reputation to travel far and your noble name to resound abroad.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見寺人一色，未識上心，或輕忽高班，凌轢貴仕，便是品命失序，綱紀不立，取笑通方之人，見譏有識之士。

translations.literal: Your subject has privately seen temple men all of one sort, not knowing the ruler's mind, sometimes slighting high ranks and trampling eminent officials—this is rank and command losing order, statutes and discipline not established, drawing laughter from those versed in the Way and drawing scorn from men of discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I see eunuchs of one kind who do not know your mind, who sometimes slight high officials and trample eminent men. Rank and discipline lose their order, and men versed in the Way laugh while men of discernment scorn what they see.

sentences.zh: 然典內職掌，唯在門外通傳；

translations.literal: Yet the duties of the inner canon are only to relay messages outside the gates;
translations.idiomatic: By regulation their duties lie only in relaying messages outside the gates;

sentences.zh: 給使主司，但緣階闥供奉。

translations.literal: the chief offices of supply and service are only to attend along the steps and gate-towers.
translations.idiomatic: and supply offices are only to attend along the steps and gate-towers.

sentences.zh: 今乃往來閣內，出入宮中，行路之人，咸以為怪。

translations.literal: Now they come and go within the pavilions and enter and leave the palace interior; travelers on the road all find it strange.
translations.idiomatic: Now they come and go within the pavilions and in and out of the inner palace. Everyone who sees it finds it strange.

sentences.zh: 伏望狎近君子，屏黜小人，上副聖心，下允眾望。

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will draw near to gentlemen and screen out petty men, above matching the sage heart and below fulfilling the multitude's hope.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that you draw near to gentlemen and drive away petty men, matching your father's heart above and the people's hope below.

sentences.zh: 承乾覽書甚不悅。

translations.literal: Chengan, on reading the letter, was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Chengan read the memorial and was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 承乾嘗驅使司馭等，不許分番，又私引突厥達哥支入宮內。

translations.literal: Chengan once drove the masters of stables and others, not permitting rotation of shifts, and also privately brought the Turk Dagozhi into the palace interior.
translations.idiomatic: Chengan once kept the stable masters and others on continuous duty without rotation, and also privately brought the Turk Dagozhi into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 志寧上書諫曰：

translations.literal: Zhining submitted a written remonstrance, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhining submitted another written remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 臣聞上天蓋高，日月以光其德；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that Heaven above is lofty, and sun and moon by their light display its virtue;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Heaven is lofty, and sun and moon display its virtue by their light;

sentences.zh: 明君至聖，輔佐以贊其功。

translations.literal: the enlightened ruler is supremely sage, and assistants by their aid complete his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: the enlightened ruler is supremely sage, and his assistants complete his achievement by their aid.

sentences.zh: 是以周誦升儲，見匡毛、畢；

translations.literal: Therefore when Zhou Song ascended the storehouse, he was rectified by Mao and Bi;
translations.idiomatic: When King Song of Zhou was made heir, he was guided by the Mao and Bi brothers;

sentences.zh: 漢盈居震，取資黃、綺。

translations.literal: when Han Ying occupied the thunder trigram, he took support from the Four Hoaryheads of Mount Shang.
translations.idiomatic: when Emperor Hui of Han stood in the heir's position, he drew support from the Four Hoaryheads of Mount Shang.

sentences.zh: 姬旦抗法於伯禽，賈生陳事於文帝。

translations.literal: Ji Dan upheld the law against Bo Qin; Jia Yi presented affairs to Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou upheld the law against Bo Qin; Jia Yi laid out his counsel before Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 莫不慇勤於端士，懇切於正人。

translations.literal: None failed to be earnest with upright scholars and sincere with correct men.
translations.idiomatic: In every case they were earnest with upright scholars and sincere with correct men.

sentences.zh: 昔鄧禹名臣，方居審諭之任；

translations.literal: Formerly Deng Yu, a famed minister, had just taken the charge of examining and instructing;
translations.idiomatic: In the past Deng Yu, a famed minister, had just taken the post of examining and instructing the heir;

sentences.zh: 疏受宿望，始除輔導之官。

translations.literal: Shu Shou, of long-standing repute, was first removed to the office of assisting and guiding.
translations.idiomatic: and Shu Shou, a man of long-standing repute, was first appointed to the office of guiding the heir.

sentences.zh: 歷代賢君，莫不丁寧於太子者，良以地膺上嗣，位處副君，善則率土沾其恩，惡則海內罹其禍。

translations.literal: Through the ages worthy rulers have all been earnest and attentive toward the crown prince, truly because he bears the position of supreme successor and stands as deputy lord—if good, then all within the bounds are moistened by his grace; if evil, then within the seas they suffer his calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy rulers of every age have been earnest with the crown prince, for he stands as supreme heir and deputy lord: if he is good, the realm shares his grace; if he is wicked, the realm suffers his calamity.

sentences.zh: 近聞僕寺、司馭，爰及駕士、獸醫，始自春初，迄茲夏晚，常居內役，不放分番。

translations.literal: Recently it is heard that the stewards' office, stable masters, and also carriage men and veterinary physicians, from the beginning of spring down to this late summer, have constantly dwelt in inner service and are not released for shift rotation.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that stewards, stable masters, carriage men, and veterinary physicians have been kept on inner duty from early spring until late summer without rotation.

sentences.zh: 或家有尊親，闕於溫凊；

translations.literal: Some have venerable kin at home and lack in warmth in cold and coolness in heat;
translations.idiomatic: Some have elderly parents at home whom they cannot tend in cold or heat;

sentences.zh: 或室有幼弱，絕於撫養。

translations.literal: some have young and weak in the household and are cut off from nurturing;
translations.idiomatic: others have young children at home whom they cannot raise;

sentences.zh: 春則廢其耕墾，夏又妨其播殖。

translations.literal: in spring they abandon plowing and opening fields, in summer they again hinder sowing and planting.
translations.idiomatic: in spring they miss the plowing season, and in summer they miss the planting season.

sentences.zh: 事乖存愛，恐致怨嗟。

translations.literal: The affair departs from preserving love; I fear it will bring forth lament and sighs.
translations.idiomatic: This runs counter to humane care and may breed resentment.

sentences.zh: 且突厥達哥支等，人面獸心，豈得以禮教期，不可以仁信待。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Turks Dagozhi and others have human faces but beast hearts—how can one expect ritual teaching of them? One cannot treat them with benevolence and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Turk Dagozhi and his kind have human faces but beastly hearts. How can one expect them to learn ritual? They cannot be treated with benevolence and trust.

sentences.zh: 心則未識於忠孝，言則莫辯其是非，近之有損於英聲，暱之無益於盛德。

translations.literal: In mind they do not yet know loyalty and filial piety; in speech they cannot distinguish right from wrong—drawing them near harms your illustrious fame, and favoring them does not benefit your flourishing virtue.
translations.idiomatic: They know neither loyalty nor filial piety in their hearts, nor can they tell right from wrong in speech. Drawing them near will harm your noble reputation; favoring them will not advance your great virtue.

sentences.zh: 引之入閣，人皆驚駭，豈臣愚識，獨用不安？

translations.literal: Bringing them into the pavilions—everyone is startled and terrified; is it only this humble subject's foolish understanding that alone feels unease?
translations.idiomatic: Bringing them into the inner quarters has startled everyone. Is it only my foolish understanding that feels uneasy?

sentences.zh: 臣下為殿下之股肱，殿下為臣下之君父，君父以存撫為務，股肱以匡救為心。

translations.literal: Your subjects are Your Highness's arms and thighs; Your Highness is your subjects' lord and father. The lord and father take preserving and comforting as their task; the arms and thighs take correction and rescue as their heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your officials are Your Highness's arms and legs; Your Highness is their lord and father. A lord and father must preserve and comfort; arms and legs must set their hearts on correction and rescue.

sentences.zh: 是以苦口之藥以奉身，逆耳之言以安位。

translations.literal: Therefore bitter medicine in the mouth is offered for the body's sake, and words that oppose the ear are spoken to secure the position.
translations.idiomatic: That is why bitter medicine is taken for the body's sake, and unwelcome words are spoken to secure one's position.

sentences.zh: 古人樹誹謗之木，以求己愆；

translations.literal: The ancients set up trees for slander in order to seek their own faults;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients set up trees for slander in order to learn their own faults;

sentences.zh: 懸敢諫之鼓，以思身過。

translations.literal: they hung drums for bold remonstrance in order to reflect on personal errors.
translations.idiomatic: and hung drums for bold remonstrance in order to reflect on their own errors.

sentences.zh: 由是從諫之主，鼎祚克昌；

translations.literal: thereby rulers who accepted remonstrance had their cauldrons and fortunes flourish;
translations.idiomatic: Rulers who accepted remonstrance saw their dynasties flourish;

sentences.zh: 愎諫之君，洪業隳墜。

translations.literal: rulers obstinate against remonstrance saw their great enterprise collapse and fall.
translations.idiomatic: while rulers obstinate against remonstrance saw their great enterprise collapse.

sentences.zh: 承乾大怒，陰遣刺客張師政、紇干承基就殺之。

translations.literal: Chengan was greatly enraged and secretly sent assassins Zhang Shizheng and Qigan Chengji to go kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Chengan flew into a rage and secretly sent the assassins Zhang Shizheng and Qigan Chengji to kill him.

sentences.zh: 二人潛入其第，見志寧寢處苫廬，竟不忍而止。

translations.literal: The two men stole into his residence and saw Zhining sleeping in a mourning hut of straw; in the end they could not bear it and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The two men stole into his residence and found Zhining in the mourning hut beside his mother's bier; they could not bring themselves to kill him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及承乾敗後，推鞫具知其事。

translations.literal: When Chengan was defeated afterward, investigation fully revealed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengan's downfall, investigation fully revealed what had happened.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂志寧曰：「知公數有規諫，事無所隱。」

translations.literal: Taizong said to Zhining, "I know you have remonstrated repeatedly, and nothing is hidden in the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said to Zhining, "I know you have remonstrated repeatedly, and nothing in this affair has been concealed."

sentences.zh: 深加勉勞。

translations.literal: He greatly encouraged and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: He greatly commended and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 右庶子令狐德棻等以無諫書，皆從貶責。

translations.literal: Right Junior Tutor Linghu Defen and others, because they had no written remonstrances, were all demoted and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Right Junior Tutor Linghu Defen and others, because they had left no written remonstrances, were all demoted and punished.

sentences.zh: 及高宗為皇太子，復授志寧太子左庶子，未幾遷侍中。

translations.literal: When Gaozong became crown prince, Zhining was again appointed left junior tutor of the crown prince, and before long was transferred to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong became crown prince, Zhining was again appointed left junior tutor of the crown prince, and before long was promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，加光祿大夫，進封燕國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui he was given the additional title grand master of splendid happiness and advanced to Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonghui (650) he was given the additional title grand master of splendid happiness and advanced to Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 二年，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year he supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 時洛陽人李弘泰坐誣告太尉長孫無忌，詔令不待時而斬決。

translations.literal: At that time Li Hongtai of Luoyang was convicted of falsely accusing Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, and an edict ordered his execution without waiting for the season.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Hongtai of Luoyang was convicted of falsely accusing Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, and an edict ordered his immediate execution.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下情篤功臣，恩隆右戚。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's affection is deep toward meritorious officials and your grace lofty toward maternal kin on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's affection runs deep toward meritorious officials, and your grace is great toward the imperial in-laws.

sentences.zh: 以無忌橫遭誣告，事並是虛，欲戮告人，以明賞罰，一以絕誣告之路，二以慰勳戚之心。

translations.literal: Because Wuji suffered false accusation without cause and the matters were all empty, you wish to execute the accuser to clarify reward and punishment—first to cut off the path of false accusation, second to comfort the hearts of meritorious kin.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhangsun Wuji was falsely accused and the charges were all groundless, you wish to execute the accuser to make reward and punishment clear—first to cut off false accusations, second to comfort the hearts of meritorious kin.

sentences.zh: 又以所犯是真，無忌便有破家之罪，今告為妄，弘泰宜戮不待時。

translations.literal: Yet if the offense charged were true, Wuji would bear the crime of destroying his house; now that the accusation is false, Hongtai should be executed without waiting for the season.
translations.idiomatic: If the charge were true, Wuji would face the crime of ruining his house. But the accusation is false, and Hongtai should be executed without delay.

sentences.zh: 且真犯之人，事當罪逆；

translations.literal: Moreover, for a person who truly offended, the matter should be treasonous crime;
translations.idiomatic: When the accused is truly guilty, the offense may amount to treason;

sentences.zh: 誣謀之類，罪唯及身。

translations.literal: for the class of false plotting, guilt reaches only the person himself.
translations.idiomatic: but in cases of false plotting, guilt reaches only the accuser himself.

sentences.zh: 以罪較量，明非惡逆，若欲依律，合待秋分。

translations.literal: Comparing the crimes by measure, it is clear this is not abominable treason; if you wish to follow the statutes, execution should wait until the autumn equinox.
translations.idiomatic: Measured by the crime, this is clearly not abominable treason. If you wish to follow the law, execution should wait until the autumn equinox.

sentences.zh: 今時屬陽和，萬物生育，而特行刑罰。

translations.literal: Now the season belongs to yang harmony and the ten thousand things are giving birth, yet you specially carry out punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Now is the season of yang harmony, when the ten thousand things are being born, yet you would specially carry out executions.

sentences.zh: 此謂傷春。

translations.literal: This is called harming spring.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is called harming spring.

sentences.zh: 竊案《左傳》聲子曰：「賞以春夏，刑以秋冬。」

translations.literal: I privately examine the Zuo Commentary, where Shengzi said, "Rewards in spring and summer, punishments in autumn and winter."
translations.idiomatic: I note that in the Zuo Commentary, Shengzi said, "Rewards in spring and summer, punishments in autumn and winter."

sentences.zh: 順天時也。

translations.literal: This follows Heaven's seasons.
translations.idiomatic: This follows Heaven's seasons.

sentences.zh: 又《禮記·月令》曰：「孟春之月，無殺孩蟲。

translations.literal: Again, the Monthly Ordinances in the Book of Rites says, "In the first month of spring, do not kill young creatures or insects.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances in the Book of Rites also says, "In the first month of spring, do not kill young creatures or insects.

sentences.zh: 省囹圄，去桎梏，無肆掠，止獄訟。」

translations.literal: Reduce prisons, remove fetters and cangues, do not permit plunder at will, and halt prison lawsuits."
translations.idiomatic: Reduce the prisons, remove fetters, forbid wanton plunder, and halt lawsuits."

sentences.zh: 又《漢書》董仲舒曰：「王者欲有所為，宜求其端於天道。

translations.literal: Again, in the Book of Han, Dong Zhongshu said, "When a king wishes to act, he should seek the beginning in the Way of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the Book of Han, Dong Zhongshu also said, "When a king wishes to act, he should seek the root of it in the Way of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天道之大者在陰陽。

translations.literal: The great part of the Way of Heaven lies in yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: The great principle of the Way of Heaven lies in yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 陽為德，陰為刑，刑主殺而德主生。

translations.literal: Yang is virtue, yin is punishment; punishment governs killing while virtue governs giving life.
translations.idiomatic: Yang is virtue, yin is punishment; punishment governs killing, while virtue governs giving life.

sentences.zh: 陽常居大夏，而以生育養長為事；

translations.literal: Yang constantly dwells in great summer and takes nourishing growth and rearing as its task;
translations.idiomatic: Yang constantly dwells in great summer and takes nurturing and growth as its task;

sentences.zh: 陰常居大冬，而積於空虛不用之處。

translations.literal: yin constantly dwells in great winter and accumulates in empty places where it is not used.
translations.idiomatic: yin constantly dwells in great winter and accumulates in empty places where it is not used.

sentences.zh: 以此見天之任德不任刑也。」

translations.literal: From this one sees that Heaven relies on virtue and does not rely on punishment."
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees that Heaven relies on virtue and not on punishment."

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下纂聖升祚，繼明御極，追連、胥之絕軌，蹈軒、頊之良規。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty has inherited sagehood and ascended the throne, continuing illumination and holding the pole, pursuing the severed tracks of Lian and Xu and treading the fine regulations of Xuan and Zhuanxu.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has inherited the sage throne and continues the enlightened rule, pursuing the lost tracks of Emperor Lian and Emperor Xu and treading the fine regulations of the Yellow Emperor and Zhuanxu.

sentences.zh: 欲使舉動順於天時，刑罰依於律令，陰陽為之式序，景宿於是靡差，風雨不愆，雩禜輟祀。

translations.literal: You wish to make every movement accord with Heaven's seasons, punishments follow statutes and orders, yin and yang serve as its pattern and sequence, the bright lodges thereby without error, wind and rain not exceeding measure, and rain-prayer and border sacrifices cease.
translations.idiomatic: You wish every movement to accord with Heaven's seasons, punishments to follow statutes, yin and yang to keep their proper order, the constellations to hold their places, wind and rain to keep their measure, and rain-prayer sacrifices to cease.

sentences.zh: 方今太蔟統律，青陽應期，當生長之辰，施肅殺之令，伏願暫回聖慮，察古人言，倘蒙垂納，則生靈幸甚。

translations.literal: Just now the great bilu sets the pitch-pipes, green yang responds to the season—it is the time of growth and birth, yet you would issue stern killing orders. I humbly hope you will for a moment turn back your sage consideration and examine the words of the ancients; if you graciously accept them, then the living masses will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Now the great bilu pitch-pipe rules and green yang answers the season—it is the time of growth, yet you would issue stern killing orders. I humbly beg that you turn your sage mind for a moment to the words of the ancients. If you accept them, the people will be greatly fortunate.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted and the emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, and the emperor accepted it.

sentences.zh: 是時，衡山公主欲出降長孫氏，議者以時既公除，合行吉禮。

translations.literal: At that time Princess Hengshan wished to go out and marry into the Zhangsun clan; debaters held that since the time had already reached public removal of mourning, auspicious rites should be performed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Princess Hengshan wished to marry into the Zhangsun clan. Some argued that since the public mourning period had ended, auspicious wedding rites should proceed.

sentences.zh: 志寧上疏曰：

translations.literal: Zhining submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Zhining submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞明君馭歷，當俟獻替之臣；

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that an enlightened ruler steering the calendar should await ministers who offer correction and replacement;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that an enlightened ruler governing the realm should await ministers who offer correction and replacement;

sentences.zh: 聖主握圖，必資鹽梅之佐。

translations.literal: a sage lord grasping the chart must rely on assistants like salt and prunus.
translations.idiomatic: and a sage lord holding the realm must rely on assistants like salt and prunus.

sentences.zh: 所以堯詢四岳，景化洽於區中；

translations.literal: Therefore Yao inquired of the Four Peaks and radiant transformation harmonized within the realm;
translations.idiomatic: Yao inquired of the Four Peaks, and radiant transformation spread through the realm;

sentences.zh: 舜任五臣，懿德被於無外。

translations.literal: Shun entrusted five ministers and fine virtue spread beyond all bounds.
translations.idiomatic: Shun entrusted five ministers, and fine virtue spread beyond all bounds.

sentences.zh: 左有記言之史，右立記事之官，大小咸書，善惡俱載。

translations.literal: On the left were historians who recorded words; on the right were established officials who recorded affairs—great and small all written, good and evil both entered.
translations.idiomatic: On the left were historians who recorded words; on the right were officials who recorded affairs. Great and small were all written down, good and evil alike recorded.

sentences.zh: 著懲勸於簡牘，垂褒貶於人倫，為萬古之範圍，作千齡之龜鏡。

translations.literal: They set punishment and encouragement on bamboo slips, let praise and blame hang down upon human relations, becoming the compass of ten thousand ages and the tortoise mirror of a thousand spans.
translations.idiomatic: They set punishment and encouragement down in writing, let praise and blame shape human conduct, and became the compass of ten thousand ages and the mirror of a thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 伏見衡山公主出降，欲就今秋成禮。

translations.literal: I humbly see that Princess Hengshan, going out to marry down, wishes to complete the rites this autumn.
translations.idiomatic: I see that Princess Hengshan is to marry and that some wish the rites completed this autumn.

sentences.zh: 竊按《禮記》云：「女十五而笄，二十而嫁；

translations.literal: I privately examine the Book of Rites, which says, "A girl at fifteen receives the hairpin, at twenty she marries;
translations.idiomatic: I note that the Book of Rites says, "A girl receives the hairpin at fifteen and marries at twenty;

sentences.zh: 有故，二十三而嫁。」

translations.literal: if there is cause, at twenty-three she marries."
translations.idiomatic: if there is cause, at twenty-three she marries."

sentences.zh: 鄭玄云：「有故，謂遭喪也。」

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said, "'If there is cause' means encountering mourning."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan said, "'If there is cause' means encountering mourning."

sentences.zh: 固知須終三年。

translations.literal: Thus one knows she must complete three years.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows she must complete the full three-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》云：「魯莊公如齊納幣。」

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals says, "Duke Zhuang of Lu went to Qi to present betrothal gifts."
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals says, "Duke Zhuang of Lu went to Qi to present betrothal gifts."

sentences.zh: 杜預云：「母喪未再期而圖婚，二傳不譏失禮，明故也。」

translations.literal: Du Yu said, "His mother's mourning had not yet reached two full years when he planned marriage; the two commentaries do not condemn this as loss of ritual—this shows there was cause."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu said, "His mother's mourning had not yet reached two full years when he planned marriage; the two commentaries do not condemn this as a breach of ritual, which shows there was cause."

sentences.zh: 此即史策具載，是非歷然，斷在聖情，不待問於臣下。

translations.literal: This is fully recorded in historical annals; right and wrong are clear through the ages. The decision lies in the sage heart and does not await inquiry from your subjects.
translations.idiomatic: This is fully recorded in the histories, and right and wrong are clear. The decision lies in Your Majesty's sage judgment and need not await inquiry from your subjects.

sentences.zh: 其有議者云：「准制，公除之後，須並從吉。」

translations.literal: There are those who debate, saying, "According to the regulations, after public removal of mourning one must altogether follow auspicious rites."
translations.idiomatic: Some argue, "According to the regulations, after public removal of mourning one must altogether follow auspicious rites."

sentences.zh: 此漢文創製其儀，為天下百姓。

translations.literal: This was instituted by Emperor Wen of Han for the common people of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: This was instituted by Emperor Wen of Han for the common people of the realm.

sentences.zh: 至於公主，服是斬縗，縱使服隨例除，無宜情隨例改。

translations.literal: As for a princess, her garment is the severest hemp; even if the garment follows precedent in removal, it is not fitting that feeling follow precedent in change.
translations.idiomatic: As for a princess, her mourning garment is the severest hemp. Even if the garment may be removed by precedent, her feeling should not change by precedent.

sentences.zh: 心喪之內，方復成婚，非唯違於禮經，亦是人情不可。

translations.literal: Within the mourning of the heart, she would again marry—this not only violates the ritual classics but is also impossible in human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: To marry again while still in the mourning of the heart violates not only the ritual classics but also what human feeling can bear.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下嗣膺寶位，臨統萬方，理宜繼美羲、軒，齊芳湯、禹，弘獎仁孝之日，敦崇名教之秋。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty has succeeded to the precious throne and oversees the ten thousand directions; by principle you should continue the beauty of Xi and Xuan, match in fragrance Tang and Yu, in the day of broadly encouraging benevolence and filial piety and in the autumn of earnestly honoring name and teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has succeeded to the throne and rules the ten thousand directions. By right you should continue the beauty of the sage rulers Xi and Xuan and match the fame of Tang and Yu, in this season of encouraging benevolence and filial piety and honoring the teachings of ritual.

sentences.zh: 此事行之苦難，猶須抑而守禮，況行之甚易，何容廢而受譏？

translations.literal: If this matter were hard to carry out, one would still have to restrain it and keep ritual; how much less when it is very easy to carry out—how can it be abandoned and receive reproach?
translations.idiomatic: If this were hard to do, one would still restrain oneself and keep ritual. How much less when it is easy—how can it be abandoned and invite reproach?

sentences.zh: 此理有識之所共知，非假愚臣之說也。

translations.literal: This principle is what men of discernment commonly know; it does not rely on this foolish subject's words.
translations.idiomatic: Men of discernment know this principle already; it does not depend on my foolish words.

sentences.zh: 伏願遵高宗之令軌，略孝文之權制，國家於法無虧，公主情禮得畢。

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will follow the ordered tracks of Emperor Gaozong, set aside the expedient regulations of Emperor Xiaowen, so that the state suffers no loss in law and the princess's feeling and ritual may be completed.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that you follow the ordered tracks of Emperor Gaozong and set aside the expedient regulations of Emperor Xiaowen, so that the state suffers no loss in law and the princess's feeling and ritual may both be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 於是詔公主待三年服闋，然後成禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the princess to wait until the three-year mourning was complete, and then complete the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict ordered the princess to wait until the three-year mourning was complete before completing the wedding rites.

sentences.zh: 其年，拜尚書左僕射、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: That year he was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and associate with the Secretariat-Chancellery at third rank.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and associate with the Secretariat-Chancellery at third rank.

sentences.zh: 三年，以本官兼太子少師。

translations.literal: In the third year he held his former office concurrently as junior tutor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he held his former office while also serving as junior tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，遷太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he was transferred to grand tutor of the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing (656) he was transferred to grand tutor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 嘗與右僕射張行成、中書令高季輔俱蒙賜地，志寧奏曰：「臣居關右，代襲箕裘，周魏以來，基址不墜。

translations.literal: Once, together with right vice director Zhang Xingcheng and director of the Secretariat Gao Jifu, he was all granted land; Zhining submitted, saying, "Your subject dwells in the region west of the Pass; generation after generation we inherit the fur robe, and from Zhou and Wei down the foundation has not fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Once he and Right Vice Director Zhang Xingcheng and Director of the Secretariat Gao Jifu were all granted land. Zhining submitted, "I dwell west of the Pass. My family has inherited its estate for generations, and from Zhou and Wei down our foundation has not fallen.

sentences.zh: 行成等新營莊宅，尚少田園，於臣有餘，乞申私讓。」

translations.literal: Xingcheng and others have newly built manor houses and still lack fields and gardens; what I have is in surplus—I beg to offer a private transfer."
translations.idiomatic: Xingcheng and the others have newly built manor houses and still lack fields and gardens. What I have is more than I need, and I beg to offer a private transfer."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其意，乃分賜行成及季輔。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his intent and thereupon divided the grant between Xingcheng and Jifu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his intent and divided the grant between Xingcheng and Jifu.

sentences.zh: 四年，表請致仕，聽解尚書左僕射，拜太子太師，仍同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he submitted a memorial requesting retirement; he was permitted to resign as left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, appointed grand tutor of the crown prince, and still associated with the Secretariat-Chancellery at third rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he requested retirement. He was permitted to resign as left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, appointed grand tutor of the crown prince, and still associated with the Secretariat-Chancellery at third rank.

sentences.zh: 高宗之將廢王庶人也。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was about to depose the Wang consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong was about to depose Consort Wang.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌、褚遂良執正不從，而李勣、許敬宗密申勸請，志寧獨無言以持兩端。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang held to rectitude and would not follow, while Li Ji and Xu Jingzong secretly urged the request; Zhining alone kept silent to hold both ends.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang held firm and would not agree, while Li Ji and Xu Jingzong secretly urged the move. Zhining alone kept silent, holding to both sides.

sentences.zh: 及許敬宗推鞫長孫無忌詔獄，因誣構志寧黨附無忌，坐是免職，尋降授榮州刺史。

translations.literal: When Xu Jingzong investigated Zhangsun Wuji in the imperial prison by edict, he thereupon falsely framed Zhining as cliquing with Wuji; because of this he was removed from office and soon demoted to prefect of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jingzong investigated Zhangsun Wuji in the imperial prison, he falsely framed Zhining as a partisan of Wuji. Zhining was removed from office and soon demoted to prefect of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 麟德元年，累轉華州刺史，年老請致仕，許之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Linde he was transferred in succession to prefect of Huazhou; old in years, he requested retirement and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Linde (664) he was transferred to prefect of Huazhou. In old age he requested retirement and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒於家，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the second year he died at home, age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died at home at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈幽州都督，謚曰定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the post of regional inspector of Youzhou; his posthumous name was Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed regional inspector of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 上元三年，追復其左光祿大夫、太子太師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shangyuan his left grand master of splendid happiness and grand tutor of the crown prince were posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Shangyuan (676) his titles of left grand master of splendid happiness and grand tutor of the crown prince were posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 志寧雅愛賓客，接引忘倦，後進文筆之士，無不影附，然亦不能有所薦達，議者以此少之。

translations.literal: Zhining by nature loved guests and received them without tiring of introduction; younger men of literary brush all attached to him like shadows, yet he also could not recommend and advance them—debators for this thought less of him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining by nature loved guests and received them tirelessly. Young men of literary talent all attached themselves to him like shadows, yet he could not recommend them for advancement, and critics thought less of him for this.

sentences.zh: 前後預撰格式律令、《五經義疏》及修禮、修史等功，賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: Before and after he took part in drafting standard formats and statutes, the Meaning and Commentary on the Five Classics, and the work of revising ritual and revising history—rewards and gifts beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in drafting standard formats and statutes, the Meaning and Commentary on the Five Classics, and the revision of ritual and history. The rewards he received were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 有集二十捲。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子立政，太僕少卿。

translations.literal: His son Lizheng was vice director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lizheng served as vice director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 志寧玄孫休烈，休烈子益，自有傳。

translations.literal: Zhining's great-great-grandson Xiulie, and Xiulie's son Yi, have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhining's great-great-grandson Xiulie and Xiulie's son Yi have their own biographies.

sentences.zh: 高季輔，德州蓚人也。

translations.literal: Gao Jifu was a man of Gao in Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jifu was a native of Gao in Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 祖表，魏安德太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Biao was prefect of Ande under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Biao served as prefect of Ande under Wei.

sentences.zh: 父衡，隋萬年令。

translations.literal: His father Heng was magistrate of Wannian under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Heng served as magistrate of Wannian under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 季輔少好學，兼習武藝。

translations.literal: Jifu in youth loved learning and also practiced martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu loved learning from youth and also practiced martial arts.

sentences.zh: 居母喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: While dwelling in mourning for his mother he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He became known for filial piety during mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 兄元道，仕隋為汲令。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yuandao served the Sui as magistrate of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yuandao served the Sui as magistrate of Ji.

sentences.zh: 武德初，縣人翻城從賊，元道被害，季輔率其黨出斗，竟擒殺其兄者，斬之持首以祭墓，甚為士友所稱。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude the county people turned the city and followed the rebels; Yuandao was harmed. Jifu led his faction out to fight, finally captured and killed the man who had killed his brother, beheaded him and carried the head to sacrifice at the tomb—greatly praised by scholar friends.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wude the county people rebelled and joined the enemy. Yuandao was killed. Jifu led his followers out to fight, captured the man who had killed his brother, beheaded him, and carried the head to sacrifice at his brother's tomb. Scholar friends praised him greatly.

sentences.zh: 由是群盜多歸附之，眾至數千。

translations.literal: Thereby many bandit groups came to attach to him, his host reaching several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Many bandit groups then attached themselves to him, and his following reached several thousand.

sentences.zh: 尋與武陟人李厚德率眾來降，授陟州總管府戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: Soon, together with Li Houde of Wuzhi, he led the masses to surrender and was appointed registrar of the household section in the Wuzhou regional commandery headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Li Houde of Wuzhi led their followers to surrender and he was appointed registrar of the household section in the Wuzhou regional headquarters.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，擢拜監察御史，多所彈糾，不避權要。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was promoted and appointed investigating censor, impeaching many matters and not avoiding the powerful and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was promoted to investigating censor. He impeached many officials and did not spare the powerful.

sentences.zh: 累轉中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 時太宗數召近臣，令指陳時政損益。

translations.literal: At the time Taizong repeatedly summoned nearby ministers and ordered them to point out gains and losses in current government.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Taizong repeatedly summoned nearby ministers and ordered them to point out what was right and wrong in current government.

sentences.zh: 季輔上封事五條：其略曰：

translations.literal: Jifu submitted a sealed report in five articles; the summary says:
translations.idiomatic: Jifu submitted a sealed report in five articles. The summary reads:

sentences.zh: 陛下平定九州，富有四海，德超邃古，道高前烈。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has pacified the Nine Provinces and is rich in the Four Seas; your virtue surpasses remote antiquity and your Way is higher than former exemplars.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has pacified the Nine Provinces and is rich in the Four Seas. Your virtue surpasses remote antiquity and your Way rises above former exemplars.

sentences.zh: 時已平矣，功已成矣，然而刑典未措者，何哉？

translations.literal: The times are already peaceful and achievements already complete—yet why are penal codes still not set aside?
translations.idiomatic: The times are already peaceful and your achievements already complete. Yet why are penal codes still not set aside?

sentences.zh: 良由謀猷之臣，不弘簡易之政；

translations.literal: Truly it is because planning ministers do not extend simple and easy government;
translations.idiomatic: Surely it is because planning ministers do not extend simple and easy government;

sentences.zh: 台閣之使，昧於經遠之道。

translations.literal: envoys of the terrace pavilions are obscure regarding the Way of enduring far.
translations.idiomatic: and envoys of the central offices are blind to the Way of lasting governance.

sentences.zh: 執憲者以深刻為奉公，當官者以侵下為益國，未有坦平恕之懷，副聖明之旨。

translations.literal: Those who uphold the law take severity as serving the public; those who hold office take encroaching on subordinates as benefiting the state—none have the open, level, and forgiving heart that matches the sage and bright intent.
translations.idiomatic: Those who uphold the law take severity as serving the public; those who hold office take encroaching on subordinates as benefiting the state. None have the open, level, and forgiving heart that matches your sage intent.

sentences.zh: 至如設官分職，各有司存。

translations.literal: As for establishing offices and dividing duties, each has its responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: As for establishing offices and dividing duties, each has its responsible office.

sentences.zh: 尚書八座，責成斯在，王者司契，義屬於茲。

translations.literal: The eight seats of the Department of State Affairs—fulfillment of responsibility lies here; the king's keeper of the tally—its meaning belongs here.
translations.idiomatic: The eight seats of the Department of State Affairs bear the responsibility for fulfillment of duty; the king's keeper of the tally has its meaning here.

sentences.zh: 伏願隨方訓誘，使各揚其職。

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will instruct and guide according to each man's place and make each display his office.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope you will instruct each according to his place and make each perform his duty.

sentences.zh: 仍須擢溫厚之人，升清潔之吏；

translations.literal: Still further you must promote men of warm thickness and elevate officials of pure cleanliness;
translations.idiomatic: You must also promote men of warm and steady character and elevate officials of pure conduct;

sentences.zh: 惇樸素，革澆浮，先之以敬讓，示之以好惡，使家識孝慈，人知廉恥。

translations.literal: honor plain simplicity, reform the watered and floating, take reverence and yielding as what comes first, show them likes and dislikes, make households know filial piety and compassion and men know integrity and shame.
translations.idiomatic: honor plain simplicity and reform shallow extravagance, lead with reverence and yielding, show them what to love and hate, until households know filial piety and compassion and men know integrity and shame.

sentences.zh: 丑言過行，見嗤於鄉閭；

translations.literal: ugly words and excessive conduct are laughed at in village lanes;
translations.idiomatic: Ugly words and bad conduct are mocked in the villages;

sentences.zh: 忘義私暱，取擯於親族。

translations.literal: forgetting righteousness for private intimacy brings rejection from kin.
translations.idiomatic: forgetting righteousness for private favor brings rejection from kin.

sentences.zh: 杜其利慾之心，載以清淨之化。

translations.literal: Block their hearts of profit and desire and carry them with pure and clean transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Block their hearts of profit and desire and carry them with pure and clean transformation.

sentences.zh: 自然家肥國富，氣和物阜。

translations.literal: Naturally households grow rich and the state grows wealthy, qi harmonizes and things flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Then households will grow rich, the state wealthy, qi will harmonize, and things will flourish.

sentences.zh: 禮節於是競興，禍亂何由而作？

translations.literal: Ritual and measure will then vie to rise—by what path could calamity and disorder arise?
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and propriety will then flourish everywhere. By what path could calamity and disorder arise?

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: Again he said:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 竊見聖躬，每存節儉，而凡諸營繕，工徒未息。

translations.literal: I privately see that Your Sage Person constantly preserves economy, yet in all construction and repair the workmen have not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: I see that Your Majesty constantly preserves economy, yet in all construction and repair the workmen have not ceased.

sentences.zh: 正丁正匠，不供驅使，和雇和市，非無勞費。

translations.literal: Regular corvée laborers and regular craftsmen are not supplied for service; hired labor and market purchases are not without labor and expense.
translations.idiomatic: Regular corvée laborers and craftsmen are not available for other service, and hired labor and market purchases are not without cost.

sentences.zh: 人主所欲，何事不成？

translations.literal: What the lord of men desires—what matter would not succeed?
translations.idiomatic: What the lord of men desires—what matter would not succeed?

sentences.zh: 猶願愛其財而勿殫，惜其力而勿竭。

translations.literal: Still I hope you will love your wealth and not exhaust it, cherish your strength and not drain it.
translations.idiomatic: Still I hope you will love your wealth and not exhaust it, cherish your strength and not drain it.

sentences.zh: 今畿內數州，實惟邦本，地狹人稠，耕植不博，菽粟雖賤，儲蓄未多，特宜優矜，令得休息。

translations.literal: Now the several prefectures within the capital region are truly the root of the state: the land is narrow and the people dense, planting and cultivation are not broad; though beans and grain are cheap, stores are not plentiful—they especially should receive favor and compassion and be allowed rest.
translations.idiomatic: The several prefectures around the capital are truly the root of the state. The land is narrow and the people dense; planting is not extensive. Though grain is cheap, stores are not plentiful. They especially deserve favor and should be allowed to rest.

sentences.zh: 強本弱枝，自古常事。

translations.literal: Strengthening the root and weakening the branches has been a constant affair since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Strengthening the root and weakening the branches has been a constant principle since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 關、河之外，徭役全少，帝京、三輔，差科非一；

translations.literal: Beyond the Pass and the Yellow River, corvée labor is altogether few; in the imperial capital and the three auxiliaries, levies of service are not one kind;
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Pass and the Yellow River, corvée labor is altogether light; in the imperial capital and the three auxiliaries, levies are many and varied;

sentences.zh: 江南、河北，彌復優閒。

translations.literal: south of the Yangzi and north of the Yellow River are still more easy and leisurely.
translations.idiomatic: and south of the Yangzi and north of the Hebei region are still more easy and leisurely.

sentences.zh: 須為差等，均其勞逸。

translations.literal: There must be graded distinctions to equalize their labor and ease.
translations.idiomatic: There must be graded distinctions to equalize their labor and ease.

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: Again he said:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 今公主之室，封邑足以給資用；

translations.literal: Now the households of princesses have enfeoffments sufficient to supply their needs;
translations.idiomatic: Now princesses' households have enfeoffments sufficient for their needs;

sentences.zh: 勳貴之家，俸祿足以供器服。

translations.literal: the homes of meritorious nobles have salaries sufficient to supply vessels and garments.
translations.idiomatic: and the homes of meritorious nobles have salaries sufficient for vessels and garments.

sentences.zh: 乃慼慼於儉約，汲汲於華侈，放息出舉，追求什一。

translations.literal: Yet they are sorrowful over economy and urgent over splendor and luxury, releasing interest and lending out, pursuing one in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they fret over economy while rushing after splendor, lending at interest and pursuing profits of one in ten.

sentences.zh: 公侯尚且求利，黎庶豈覺其非？

translations.literal: If dukes and marquises still seek profit, how would the common people perceive it as wrong?
translations.idiomatic: If dukes and marquises still seek profit, how would the common people know it is wrong?

sentences.zh: 錐刀必競，實由於此，有黷朝風，謂宜懲革。

translations.literal: The awl and knife must compete—this truly comes from this; it profanes court style, and I say it should be punished and reformed.
translations.idiomatic: The scramble for petty profit comes from this. It profanes court style, and I say it should be punished and reformed.

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: Again he said:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 仕以應務代耕，外官卑品，猶未得祿，既離鄉家，理必貧匱。

translations.literal: Office is to respond to affairs in place of farming; outer officials of low rank still do not receive salary—having left home districts, by principle they must be poor and lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Office is to respond to affairs in place of farming. Outer officials of low rank still receive no salary. Having left their home districts, they must by nature be poor.

sentences.zh: 但妻子之戀，賢達猶累其懷；

translations.literal: Yet the longing for wife and children—even the worthy and accomplished are still burdened in their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: Yet longing for wife and children—even the worthy are burdened in their hearts;

sentences.zh: 飢寒之切，夷、惠罕全其行。

translations.literal: the urgency of hunger and cold—Bo Yi and Liu Xiahui rarely preserved their conduct intact.
translations.idiomatic: and the urgency of hunger and cold—men like Bo Yi and Liu Xiahui rarely preserved their conduct intact.

sentences.zh: 為政之道，期於易從。

translations.literal: The Way of governing affairs is expected to be easy to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of governing should be easy to follow.

sentences.zh: 若不恤其匱乏，唯欲責其清勤，凡在末品，中庸者多，止恐巡察歲去，輶軒繼軌。

translations.literal: If you do not relieve their poverty and lack but only wish to demand their purity and diligence, all who are in the lowest ranks—most are middling and ordinary—I fear only that when inspection tours depart year by year, light carriages follow in their tracks.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not relieve their poverty but only demand purity and diligence, most of the lowest ranks are middling men. I fear only that when inspection tours depart each year, light carriages will follow in their tracks.

sentences.zh: 不能肅其侵漁，何以求其政術？

translations.literal: If you cannot make severe their encroachment and fishing, how can you seek their governmental skill?
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot stop their encroachment and extortion, how can you seek good government from them?

sentences.zh: 今戶口漸殷，倉廩已實，斟量給祿，使得養親。

translations.literal: Now households are gradually abundant and granaries already full—weigh and measure granting salaries so they may support their parents.
translations.idiomatic: Now households are growing abundant and granaries are full. Weigh and grant salaries so they may support their parents.

sentences.zh: 然後督以嚴科，責其報效，則庶官畢力，物議斯允。

translations.literal: Then afterward supervise them with strict statutes and demand their repayment in service—then the multitude of officials will exhaust their strength and public opinion will approve.
translations.idiomatic: Then supervise them with strict statutes and demand their service in return. Then officials will give their full strength and public opinion will approve.

sentences.zh: 又曰：

translations.literal: Again he said:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 竊見密王元曉等，俱是懿親，陛下友愛之懷，義高古昔，分以車服，委以籓維，須依禮儀，以副瞻望。

translations.literal: I privately see that Prince Mi Yuanxiao and others are all close imperial kin; Your Majesty's heart of friendly love is righteous and higher than antiquity. You have apportioned carriages and robes and entrusted them with frontier defense—they must follow ritual and measure to match what is looked up to.
translations.idiomatic: I see that Prince Mi Yuanxiao and others are all close imperial kin. Your Majesty's heart of friendly love rises above antiquity. You have given them carriages and robes and entrusted them with frontier defense. They must follow ritual to match what the realm expects.

sentences.zh: 比見帝子拜諸叔，諸叔亦答拜，王爵既同，家人有禮，豈合如此顛倒昭穆？

translations.literal: Recently I have seen imperial sons bow to their various uncles, and the uncles also return the bow. Princely ranks being equal, there is family ritual—but how can it be fitting to so invert zhao and mu?
translations.idiomatic: Recently I have seen imperial sons bow to their uncles, and the uncles return the bow. Though princely ranks are equal, family ritual still has order. How can zhao and mu be so inverted?

sentences.zh: 伏願一垂訓誡，永循彝則。

translations.literal: I humbly hope you will let fall instruction and admonition once and forever follow the constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that you issue instruction once and forever follow the constant rule.

sentences.zh: 書奏，太宗稱善。
